$comment: A worked example: the Jira-driven agent workflow claude-monitor used to
have hardcoded. Copy this to claude-deck.config.json at the repo root and
edit it, or delete the parts you don't use — every key is optional.
Nothing here is required to run: with no config file at all you get the
session dashboard, transcripts, costs and terminals.
$comment_tag: What a tag looks like. A tag is the short identifier a session belongs to;
it ties a container name, a session's opening prompt, and a tracker item
together. The default is this Jira/Linear key shape, so you only need this
key if your scheme differs (e.g. "#\\d+" for GitHub issues).
$comment_launchers: What the Start development dialog can run. Each entry is a command of
yours with {{tag}} substituted; claude-deck owns no part of what it does.
Omit this key entirely and the dialog is simply absent.

launchers.label: Start development
launchers.description: Builds and starts an agent container on this machine.

launchers.label: Run on the shared VM
launchers.description: Starts the same container on the shared VM instead.

$comment_workflow: How to read the per-item artifact directories under SESSIONS_DIR — one
subdirectory per tag, written by your own agent workflow as it works.
A phase is done when its signal file exists and is non-empty.
"linear": false                       a side track that never blocks
Reaching a later linear phase implies the earlier ones, so a workflow that
skips a step doesn't show as stuck at it forever.
